description: TerraNova Team focuses on using AI, satellite technology and geospatial data to address agricultural challenges. Through Agroscope AI, we combine NASA data, interactive maps and AI-powered insights to help users understand agricultural conditions, identify potential risks and support better-informed decisions. Our vision is to make agriculture smarter through innovation and technology.
summary: AGROSCOPE AI is an integrated agricultural intelligence platform developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 – Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data. It brings together NASA Earth-observation resources, environmental datasets, geospatial visualization and AI-assisted interpretation to make complex environmental information more accessible. The platform features nine specialized modules, including Earth Explorer, Satellite Change Detective, Field Intelligence, Smart Water Intelligence, Crop Phenology Tracker, Farmer Action Copilot and Farm Futures Lab. Users can explore satellite imagery, investigate environmental indicators, examine historical changes and test hypothetical rainfall, temperature and irrigation scenarios. By connecting fragmented scientific resources with interactive analysis and accessible explanations, AGROSCOPE AI helps users better understand environmental conditions and explore potential climate-resilient agricultural adaptation strategies. It aims to bridge the gap between Earth-observation data and informed agricultural exploration.
details:
AGROSCOPE AI — Project Details

1. Project Overview

AGROSCOPE AI is an integrated agricultural intelligence platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, under the challenge "Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data."

The central objective of AGROSCOPE AI is to bridge the gap between complex Earth-observation data and accessible agricultural intelligence. Agriculture is strongly influenced by environmental factors such as rainfall variability, temperature fluctuations, soil-moisture conditions and vegetation dynamics. Although NASA provides valuable Earth-observation and environmental datasets, accessing, connecting and interpreting these resources can be challenging for users who need location-specific environmental understanding.

AGROSCOPE AI addresses this challenge by bringing together NASA data resources, environmental analysis, geospatial visualization, historical exploration and artificial intelligence within a unified interactive platform.

Rather than presenting isolated datasets, the platform provides a connected workflow through which users can explore geographical regions, investigate environmental conditions, compare observations across time, understand analytical findings and explore hypothetical agricultural adaptation scenarios.

The platform follows four fundamental stages:

OBSERVE → ANALYZE → INTERPRET → ADAPT

Its goal is to make Earth-observation intelligence more accessible and useful for farmers, agricultural researchers, environmental analysts and agricultural planners.

2. What Does AGROSCOPE AI Do?

AGROSCOPE AI provides a modular environment for exploring environmental conditions and investigating their potential agricultural implications.

Users can select geographical locations, explore available satellite imagery, examine environmental indicators, investigate historical patterns and use AI-assisted interpretation to understand the available information.

The platform also includes an interactive scenario exploration environment where users can modify hypothetical environmental parameters, including rainfall, temperature and irrigation inputs, to investigate how selected analytical indicators respond to different conditions.

The complete experience is organized around nine specialized modules.

A. Earth Observation and Geospatial Exploration

1. Earth Explorer

Earth Explorer provides an interactive geographical workspace for navigating different regions and exploring available NASA satellite imagery. It allows users to examine geographical locations, investigate imagery layers and establish spatial context for further environmental analysis.

2. Satellite Change Detective

Satellite Change Detective enables multi-temporal satellite imagery exploration. Users can compare imagery from selected dates and investigate visible geographical and environmental differences across different observation periods.

This capability helps users explore changes in selected regions rather than depending on a single static satellite image.

3. Field Boundary Intelligence

Field Boundary Intelligence focuses on geographical field boundaries and parcel geometries. It allows users to explore selected field areas alongside available environmental information, providing a more focused spatial perspective for agricultural analysis.

B. Environmental and Agricultural Intelligence

4. Field Intelligence

Field Intelligence provides a location-based environmental analysis workspace. It brings together available agricultural and environmental indicators to help users investigate conditions associated with a selected geographical location.

5. Smart Water Intelligence

Smart Water Intelligence focuses on precipitation and soil-moisture indicators. It helps users investigate water-related environmental conditions and explore information relevant to agricultural water-resource assessment.

6. Crop Phenology Tracker

Crop Phenology Tracker provides vegetation and seasonal exploration capabilities. It visualizes available vegetation trends across selected periods and helps users investigate changes in vegetation observations in relation to environmental conditions.

7. Regional Risk Radar

Regional Risk Radar brings together available environmental indicators to support geographical vulnerability exploration. It helps users identify regions that may deserve further investigation based on the available analytical information.

C. AI-Assisted Intelligence and Future Exploration

8. Farmer Action Copilot

Farmer Action Copilot is an AI-assisted interpretation module powered by Gemini 2.5 Flash through OpenRouter.

It helps transform available environmental information into accessible explanations, connects analytical findings with geographical context and helps users investigate potential agricultural adaptation approaches.

The Copilot is intended to support understanding rather than replace scientific validation or professional agricultural advice. Its interpretation should distinguish available evidence, assumptions and uncertainty.

9. Farm Futures Lab

Farm Futures Lab is an interactive environmental scenario exploration environment.

Users can experiment with hypothetical changes in rainfall, temperature and irrigation parameters and investigate how these changes influence selected analytical indicators.

Instead of presenting these scenarios as guaranteed predictions, the module provides an environment for exploring possible conditions, comparing inputs and understanding environmental sensitivity.

Additional Platform Capabilities

In addition to the nine specialized modules, AGROSCOPE AI includes supporting capabilities such as:

  • Satellite Time Machine for historical satellite observation exploration.
  • Historical Environmental Analysis for investigating environmental patterns across selected periods.
  • Interactive Geospatial Visualization for location-based exploration.
  • Reports and Exportable Insights for presenting and sharing available analytical findings.

The major strength of the platform is the relationship between these capabilities. Users can move from geographical observation to environmental investigation, historical comparison, AI-assisted interpretation and hypothetical adaptation exploration within one connected experience.

3. How Does the System Work?

AGROSCOPE AI follows an integrated data-to-intelligence workflow.

Stage 1 — Data Collection and Retrieval

The platform uses NASA Earth-observation and environmental resources, including NASA POWER, NASA MERRA-2 and NASA Global Imagery Browse Services (GIBS). OpenStreetMap provides geographical mapping context.

These resources contribute different forms of environmental and geographical information.

Stage 2 — Data Processing and Integration

Python-based processing workflows support environmental data retrieval, processing, transformation and organization.

Geospatial processing supports geographical coordinates and location-based exploration. This stage helps organize information obtained from different services for use by the application.

Stage 3 — Backend Services

FastAPI provides backend API services that connect data-processing workflows with the frontend.

These services facilitate communication between application components and provide structured access to environmental and analytical information.

Stage 4 — Environmental Visualization

The frontend presents information through interactive maps, analytical charts and geographical exploration interfaces.

Users can investigate environmental indicators, explore satellite imagery and examine information associated with selected locations and time periods.

Stage 5 — AI-Assisted Interpretation

Gemini 2.5 Flash, accessed through OpenRouter, powers the AI-assisted interpretation layer.

This layer helps communicate available analytical information in understandable language and provides contextual explanations to support environmental exploration.

Stage 6 — Adaptation Scenario Exploration

Farm Futures Lab enables users to experiment with hypothetical environmental conditions and compare how selected analytical indicators respond to different input parameters.

The overall workflow can be represented as:

NASA Earth Observation and Geographic Resources
→ Data Retrieval and API Integration
→ Python-Based Processing and Geospatial Analysis
→ FastAPI Backend Services
→ Interactive Visualization
→ AI-Assisted Interpretation
→ Agricultural Intelligence and Scenario Exploration.

4. Technologies, Tools and Resources Used

AGROSCOPE AI combines modern web development technologies, backend services, scientific data resources, geospatial visualization and artificial intelligence.

Scientific Data Sources

NASA POWER: Provides meteorological and environmental parameters used to explore rainfall-related conditions, temperature patterns and other agroclimatic variables.

NASA MERRA-2: Provides historical atmospheric and environmental information through NASA's global reanalysis system, supporting the exploration of atmospheric conditions and temporal patterns.

NASA GIBS: NASA Global Imagery Browse Services provides access to visual Earth-observation products through map-compatible imagery services, supporting interactive satellite visualization.

OpenStreetMap: Provides geographical mapping information for location-based navigation and spatial context.

Backend and Data Processing

  • Python: Environmental data retrieval, processing, transformation and analytical workflows.
  • FastAPI: Backend API development and communication between data-processing services and the frontend.
  • Geospatial Processing: Coordinate handling, geographical context and location-based exploration.

Artificial Intelligence

  • OpenRouter: Provides access to the AI model used by the platform.
  • Gemini 2.5 Flash: Supports AI-assisted environmental interpretation and contextual explanations.

Frontend and Visualization

  • Next.js 16: Application framework and frontend architecture.
  • React 19: Component-based user interface development.
  • TypeScript: Structured application development and type safety.
  • Leaflet: Interactive maps, geographical navigation and satellite imagery exploration.
  • Recharts: Analytical charts and environmental data visualization.
  • Three.js: Interactive three-dimensional visualization experiences.

These technologies work together to connect scientific information, backend processing, interactive exploration and AI-assisted interpretation in one application.

5. What Makes AGROSCOPE AI Creative and Innovative?

The innovation of AGROSCOPE AI lies in connecting multiple aspects of agricultural environmental intelligence rather than treating them as separate tools.

1. Unified Earth-Observation Workspace

The platform connects multiple NASA data resources and geographical capabilities in one application environment. This reduces the need to navigate disconnected scientific services when exploring a selected region.

2. Multi-Temporal Satellite Exploration

Satellite Change Detective connects imagery exploration with historical comparison. Users can investigate visible differences across selected dates, providing a more meaningful way to examine environmental changes over time.

3. Location-Aware Environmental Intelligence

The platform organizes environmental exploration around selected geographical locations. This connects analytical information with spatial context instead of presenting only generic environmental explanations.

4. AI-Assisted Interpretation

Farmer Action Copilot introduces an accessible interpretation layer that helps users understand complex environmental information. It connects analytical findings with geographical context and communicates relevant assumptions and uncertainties.

5. Interactive Agricultural Scenario Exploration

Farm Futures Lab allows users to modify hypothetical rainfall, temperature and irrigation inputs and investigate how selected indicators respond. This introduces an interactive approach to exploring possible environmental conditions.

6. Modular and Connected Architecture

The nine specialized modules address different aspects of environmental intelligence while contributing to a broader workflow. The platform connects observation, analysis, interpretation and adaptation exploration within a unified experience.

The creative direction of AGROSCOPE AI is to move beyond displaying environmental data and provide an integrated environment for investigating what that information may mean.

6. Benefits and Intended Impact

AGROSCOPE AI aims to make Earth-observation intelligence more accessible and useful for different groups involved in agriculture and environmental analysis.

For Farmers

The platform provides a more accessible way to explore environmental information relevant to selected geographical locations. It can help users investigate rainfall-related conditions, soil-moisture indicators, vegetation trends and potential adaptation approaches.

For Agricultural Researchers

It provides an integrated environment for exploring satellite imagery, environmental indicators, geographical information and historical patterns. This can support environmental investigation and comparative analysis.

For Agricultural Planners

Regional environmental exploration can help planners investigate geographical conditions and identify potential areas that may require further attention.

For Environmental and Climate Analysts

The platform provides connected geospatial and temporal exploration capabilities for investigating environmental changes and examining possible climate-related implications.

Broader Intended Impact

  • Democratize access to NASA Earth-observation intelligence.
  • Reduce the complexity of exploring multiple environmental datasets.
  • Connect satellite observations with contextual interpretation.
  • Encourage data-informed agricultural adaptation exploration.
  • Improve accessibility of scientific environmental visualization.
  • Support awareness of environmental variability and potential agricultural vulnerabilities.

The platform is designed as a decision-support and exploration tool. Its potential value lies in helping people investigate available information and understand environmental conditions more effectively, rather than claiming guaranteed improvements in agricultural productivity.

7. Engineering Challenges and Factors Considered

Developing AGROSCOPE AI required consideration of scientific data, geographical consistency, application architecture, external services and responsible AI interpretation.

Heterogeneous Data Integration

Different NASA data services provide information through different interfaces, formats and temporal structures. Integrating these resources required coordinated retrieval, processing and presentation workflows.

Geospatial Coordinate Consistency

Maintaining consistent geographical coordinates and map representations across interconnected modules was essential for reliable location-based exploration.

Satellite Imagery and Map Rendering

Building interactive satellite map experiences required careful handling of imagery layers, geographical navigation, map states and frontend rendering.

External API Reliability

The platform depends on external data services and APIs. Response delays, retrieval failures and service limitations had to be considered when designing application workflows.

AI Interpretation and Scientific Grounding

AI-generated explanations must remain connected to available environmental information. The platform's approach emphasizes communicating evidence, assumptions and uncertainty instead of presenting unsupported AI-generated conclusions as scientific facts.

Scientific Limitations and Responsible Communication

Retrieved environmental information, derived indicators, heuristic assessments and hypothetical scenario outputs are treated as different categories of information.

The platform does not claim that its analytical outputs are independently validated farm-level measurements, guaranteed crop-yield predictions or substitutes for professional agricultural recommendations. Scenario results are intended for exploration, not as validated forecasts.

8. Development and Implementation

AGROSCOPE AI was developed over an intensive eight-day execution cycle.

The development process involved:

  • Establishing the system architecture and technical foundation.
  • Integrating NASA data resources and geographical services.
  • Developing the frontend and backend application components.
  • Implementing geospatial exploration and satellite visualization.
  • Integrating AI-assisted interpretation.
  • Developing environmental analysis and scenario exploration capabilities.
  • Addressing integration challenges and refining the connected platform.

The development approach focused on bringing scientific data resources, application services, visualization and AI capabilities together into one coherent agricultural intelligence experience.

9. Future Development Opportunities

AGROSCOPE AI provides a foundation for further development in agricultural and environmental intelligence.

Potential future improvements include:

  • Integrating additional NASA Earth-observation datasets and environmental variables.
  • Expanding crop-specific environmental analysis.
  • Improving historical and regional comparison capabilities.
  • Strengthening validation of environmental indicators using appropriate reference datasets.
  • Improving scientific evaluation of hypothetical scenario outputs.
  • Expanding location-specific agricultural exploration.
  • Further improving AI interpretation through stronger evidence grounding and uncertainty communication.
  • Developing more accessible decision-support experiences for agricultural users.

10. Project Links

Live Application:
https://agroscope-ai-nine.vercel.app/

Backend Service:
https://agroscope-ai.onrender.com/

GitHub Repository:
https://github.com/pratham655/agroscope-ai

Conclusion

AGROSCOPE AI aims to bridge the gap between the availability of Earth-observation data and the ability to explore, understand and apply that information to agricultural adaptation.

By connecting NASA environmental resources, geospatial exploration, analytical visualization, AI-assisted interpretation and interactive scenario testing, the platform creates a unified environment for investigating agricultural and environmental conditions.

Its guiding principle is simple:

Make scientific intelligence accessible without compromising accuracy, transparency or responsible interpretation.

AGROSCOPE AI — Observe. Anticipate. Adapt.
